name: Sancerre

rules.yield_base: 65 hl/ha for white, 63 for rosé, 59 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
keyfacts: Red and rosé Sancerre gained AOC status in 1959.

notes: Classic Sancerre blanc is bone dry and highly aromatic, with intense flavors of peach and gooseberry.
It has naturally high acidity and can show flinty, gunflint notes as well as citrus and spice.
Kimmeridgian marl gives powerful Sancerre, limestone gives elegant wines, and flinty clay gives wines with white and yellow flower notes.
Red Sancerre, from Pinot Noir, is light to medium bodied and floral, and the rosés are dry with raspberry and strawberry notes.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the eastern Loire, highly regarded for white wine from Sauvignon Blanc. Red and rosé are also made from Pinot Noir. White Sancerre was one of the original AOCs of 1936.
